To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a fully-automated pipeline for quantification and quality control of WMH burden in a clinical large-scale setting, (2) we show that the pipeline can be successfully applied to a large-scale clinical multi-center AIS cohort, and (3) we demonstrate that the pipeline is capable of detecting age-related changes of WMH burden.

We developed and validated a fully automated pipeline to quantify WMH burden on FLAIR MRI in large-scale clinical AIS cohorts, which includes a brain extraction algorithm and a WMH segmentation algorithm based on a convolutional autoencoder.

(1) a novel brain extraction algorithm outperforms state of the art methods on clinical images, (2) the resulting brain masks are suitable for quality control of preprocessing steps and can be used for total brain volume computation, (3) a novel WMH segmentation algorithm can be used to compute WMH volumes in clinical studies, and (4) WMH burden increases with age.
